note: BLM campground on the California bank of the Colorado River's Parker Strip, between Parker and Parker Dam; sandy riverside sites with a camp host. Reach it from the Parker side, as trailers and oversized vehicles may not cross Parker Dam. The Crossroads OHV open area is nearby; off-road vehicles must be trailered inside the campground. --Claude
summary: Crossroads (BLM, Lake Havasu FO): $5 FCFS confirmed; rec.gov facility 274288 exists but sells nothing (all sites non-reservable, rates end 2021) -> reservable false / fcfs always stands; 26 sites, max 50 ft, sites 3/14/15/16 too small for RVs; vault toilet, no water, no dump; max stay 14. Riverfront kept (sites 10-11 on open sand ~15-20 m from the river). Note corrected (Lake Havasu FO, not Needles). Phone empty -> (928) 505-1200.
flags: WATERFRONT riverfront confirmed: sites 10 and 11 (34.21132,-114.21429 and 34.21122,-114.21437) sit ~15-20 m from the Colorado River (~250 m wide) over open sand with scattered tamarisk, low bank (BLM photo shows a table on level sand a few metres above the water); sites 12-14 ~20-30 m behind broken shrubs. All sites are sold by the night ($5, first-come). Sites 15-19 are behind a continuous tree/reed strip and 20-26 are well back - so only the north-end sites are on the water; caveat worth adding to the waterfront evidence.

OHV CHECK (not a drop): the campground is beside the Crossroads OHV Open Area and BLM mentions 'great access to ... off-roading', but it is a general riverfront campground (no staging role stated; OHVs must be trailered inside). Reviewer's call; I read it as not an OHV staging camp.
RECREATION.GOV: a facility page (274288) exists with a 26-site catalog, but nothing is reservable and the BLM page says first-come; the rec.gov notices (COVID host leave, 2021 rates) are stale.
DAM ROUTE: 'Oversized vehicles and vehicles towing trailers are not permitted to cross the dam' - approach from Parker (7 miles); not a drop (the Parker route is ordinary paved highway).
